dialect.detail: JMA ORCA (Japan Medical Association standard receipt software) running on Linux, compiled with GnuCOBOL. No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL/CICS, consistent with open-source GnuCOBOL usage on Linux.
evidence: 35 COPY statements, 67 CALLs typical of GnuCOBOL modular style

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance billing (receipt/claim calculation) — specifically inpatient (nyuuin) patient co-payment and public expense burden calculation sub-program for the JMA ORCA medical receipt system
purpose.summary: ORCS02 is a subprogram within the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system that calculates patient co-payment amounts and public subsidy burdens for inpatient claims. It handles complex Japanese health insurance rules including elderly patient thresholds, regional public expense programs, meal/living expense charges, and various special insurance combinations. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2002–2008 covering numerous prefectural and national insurance rule changes.

notable_features: No FILE SECTION entries (pure calculation subprogram)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
No COMP-3 usage despite financial calculations
35 COPY statements for shared data structures
67 CALL statements to other ORCA modules
465 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
Japanese EUC-JP encoded comments (latin-1 decoded with mojibake)
Extensive revision history (100+ revisions) in header comments
Fixed-format source with some lines exceeding column 72
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments are actually EUC-JP encoded Japanese text, appearing as mojibake. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system. Source truncated at 16000 chars but mechanical indicators confirm ~992KB / 19850 lines total. No COMP-3 is unusual for financial calculations but consistent with GnuCOBOL ORCA codebase style.
